{{short description|Data analytics  approach}}

'''Augmented Analytics''' is an approach of data analytics that employs the use of [[machine learning]] and [[natural language processing]] to automate analysis processes normally done by a specialist or [[Data science|data scientist]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://emtemp.gcom.cloud/ngw/eventassets/en/conferences/bi13a/documents/gartner-data-analytics-australia-augmented-analytics-2018.pdf|title=Augmented Analytics Is the Future of Data and Analytics|last1=Sallam|first1=Rita|last2=Howson|first2=Cindi|date=July 27, 2017|website=Gartner|last3=Idoine|first3=Carlie}}</ref> The term was introduced in 2017 by Rita Sallam, Cindi Howson, and Carlie Idoine in a Gartner research paper.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gartner.com/en/information-technology/glossary/augmented-analytics|title=Definition of Augmented Analytics - Gartner Information Technology Glossary|website=Gartner}}</ref>

Augmented analytics is based on [[business intelligence]] and analytics.<ref name="PribisalićJugo2019">{{cite book|last1=Pribisalić|first1=Marko|last2=Jugo|first2=Igor|last3=Martinčić-Ipšić|first3=Sanda|title=Humanizing Technology for a Sustainable Society|chapter=Selecting a Business Intelligence Solution that is Fit for Business Requirements|year=2019|pages=443–465|doi=10.18690/978-961-286-280-0.24|isbn=9789612862800|s2cid=202767869|url=https://aisel.aisnet.org/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1023&context=bled2019}}</ref> In the graph extraction step, data from different sources are investigated.<ref name="Ghrab Romero Jouili Skhiri 2018 pp. 3–18">{{cite book | last1=Ghrab | first1=Amine | last2=Romero | first2=Oscar | last3=Jouili | first3=Salim | last4=Skhiri | first4=Sabri | series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science | volume=11031 | title=Big Data Analytics and Knowledge Discovery | chapter=Graph BI & Analytics: Current State and Future Challenges | publisher=Springer International Publishing | location=Cham | year=2018 | isbn=978-3-319-98538-1 | issn=0302-9743 | doi=10.1007/978-3-319-98539-8_1 | pages=3–18| hdl=2117/127964 }}</ref>

== Defining Augmented Analytics ==

* Machine Learning – a systematic computing method that uses algorithms to sift through data to identify relationships, trends, and patterns. It is a process that allows algorithms to dynamically learn from data instead of having a set base of programmed rules.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/high-tech/our-insights/an-executives-guide-to-machine-learning|title=An executive's guide to machine learning|last1=Pyle|first1=Dorian|last2=San Jose|first2=Cristina|date=June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.answerrocket.com/augmented-analytics/|title=What is Augmented Analytics (And How Can it Help?) {{!}} AnswerRocket|date=8 February 2019|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref>
* [[Natural language generation]] (NLG) – a software capability that takes [[unstructured data]] and translates it into plain-English, readable, language.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://narrativescience.com/what-is-natural-language-generation/|title=What is natural language generation? {{!}} Narrative Science|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref>
* Automating Insights – using machine learning algorithms to automate data analysis processes.<ref name=":0" />
* Natural Language Query – enabling users to query data using business terms that are either typed onto a search box or spoken.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/encyclopedia/term/natural-language-query|title = Definition of natural language query}}</ref>

== Data Democratization ==
Data Democratization is the democratizing data access in order to relieve data congestion and get rid of any sense of data "gatekeepers". This process must be implemented alongside a method for users to make sense of the data. This process is used in hopes of speeding up company decision making and uncovering opportunities hidden in data.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bernardmarr/2017/07/24/what-is-data-democratization-a-super-simple-explanation-and-the-key-pros-and-cons/#5a7eae4f6013|title=What is Data Democratization? A Super Simple Explanation and The Key Pros And Cons|last=Marr|first=Bernard|date=July 24, 2017|website=Forbes}}</ref>

There are three aspects to democratising data:

# Data Parameterisation and Characterisation.
# Data Decentralisation using an OS of blockchain and DLT technologies, as well as an independently governed secure data exchange to enable trust.
# Consent Market-driven Data Monetisation.

When it comes to connecting assets, there are two features that will accelerate the adoption and usage of data democratisation: decentralized identity management and business data object monetization of data ownership. It enables multiple individuals and organizations to identify, authenticate, and authorize participants and organizations, enabling them to access services, data or systems across multiple networks, organizations, environments, and use cases. It empowers users and enables a personalized, self-service digital onboarding system so that users can self-authenticate without relying on a central administration function to process their information. Simultaneously, decentralized identity management ensures the user is authorized to perform actions subject to the system’s policies based on their attributes (role, department, organization, etc.) and/ or physical location.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://eya.global/insights/democratisation-of-object-data-within-the-telecoms-sector | title=Democratisation of Object Data within the Telecoms Sector }}</ref>

== Use cases ==

*  Agriculture  – Farmers collect data on water use, soil temperature, moisture content and crop growth, augmented analytics can be used to make sense of this data and possibly identify insights that the user can then use to make business decisions.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dataversity.net/augmented-analytics-use-cases/|title=Augmented Analytics Use Cases|last=Ghosh|first=Paramita|date=June 20, 2018|website=Dataversity}}</ref>
*  Smart Cities  – Many cities across the United States, known as [[Smart city|Smart Cities]] collect large amounts of data on a daily basis. Augmented analytics can be used to simplify this data in order to increase effectiveness in city management (transportation, natural disasters, etc.).<ref name=":1" />
*  Analytic Dashboards  – Augmented analytics has the ability to take large data sets and create highly interactive and informative analytical dashboards that assist in many organizational decisions.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Howson|first1=Cindi|last2=Richardson|first2=James|last3=Sallam|first3=Rita|last4=Kronz|first4=Austin|date=February 11, 2019|title=Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms|url=https://cadran-analytics.nl/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/2019-Gartner-Magic-Quadrant-for-Analytics-and-Business-Intelligence-Platforms.pdf|journal=Gartner}}</ref>
*  Augmented Data Discovery  – Using an augmented analytics process can assist organizations in automatically finding, visualizing and narrating potentially important data correlations and trends.<ref name=":2" />
*  [[Data preparation|Data Preparation]]  – Augmented analytics platforms have the ability to take large amounts of data and organize and "clean" the data in order for it to be usable for future analyses.<ref name=":0" />
*  Business   – Businesses collect large amounts of data, daily. Some examples of types of data collected in business operations include; sales data, consumer behavior data, distribution data. An augmented analytics platform provides access to analysis of this data, which could be used in making business decisions.<ref name=":0" />
